newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government talks to unions to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government talks to unions to end strike.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government resumed talks with trade unions on Thursday in renewed efforts to end a three-week strike by nurses and doctors which has paralysed the public health service.

Morgan Tsvangirayi, secretary-general of the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU), said discussions started late on Wednesday, just hours after three cabinet ministers had vowed the government of President Robert Mugabe would maintain its tough stance against the strikers.

"We held some talks with (Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister, Florence) Chitauro...and we are meeting again now to see how we can resolve this crisis," he said of the ZCTU, which tried unsuccessfully during the week to call a nationwide strike to press the government to solve the issue.
"We made our point and the government knows there is no solution except to negotiate," Tsvangirayi said.
Chitauro -- who returned to work from leave on Wednesday -- was unavailable for comment. Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira was acting in her place in the past three weeks.

Despite growing public pressure, the government had refused to negotiate with the nurses, who went on strike on October 21 and were joined last week by doctors to demand higher pay and improved working conditions.
It has been accusing its opponents, notably veteran opposition leader Ndabaningi Sithole, of using the strikers to undermine its authority.The political opponents deny this.
The nurses and doctors strike has led to the closure of some major hospitals, and relatives say to many deaths due lack of care. The government denies the death rate has risen.

Shamuyarira -- who has been insisting all strikers have been sacked -- told reporters this week that only a 1,000 of 14,000 state-employed nurses and 100 of 800 doctors were on strike. Unions say 10,000 nurses and 500 doctors walked out.
